                        </ns0:gap>hach</ns0:hi> is thus interpreted, but why <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> is called <ns0:hi>Sheshach</ns0:hi> is an harder question and not easily resolved. Those who think the Prophet gives <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> here another name to avoid an odium from the King of <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> at this time their Enemy, neither consider the usual courage of this Prophet, nor that he speaks plainly enough <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 51.14. where he mention<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth both <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sheshach,</ns0:hi> and expoundeth the latter by the former. It is thought that <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> is called <ns0:hi>Sheshach</ns0:hi> from the name of an Idol called <ns0:hi>Shach</ns0:hi> which they worshipped, to whose ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nor they yearly kept a Festival for five days together, which they called <ns0:hi>Shace,</ns0:hi> and they say that during this festival <ns0:hi>Cyrus</ns0:hi> took <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> But these are all incertain guesses, it is enough for us to know that by the King of <ns0:hi>Sheshach</ns0:hi> is meant the King of <ns0:hi>Babel,</ns0:hi> as the Prophet expounds himself, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 51.41.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:35" />27 Therefore thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Hab. 2.16.</ns0:note> Drink ye and be drunken, and spue, and fall, and rise no more, because of the sword which I will send amongst you.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And it shall be if they refuse to take the cup at thine hand to drink, then shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Ye shall certainly drink <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The meaning of these two verses is no more then this, God let <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> in a Vision know that it was his will, that he should prophesie a certain, and inavoidable ruine to all these Nations, which was brought upon all the rest by the King of <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> whom God made his instrument to execute his vengeance upon them: and last of all upon the King of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> himself by <ns0:hi>Cyrus</ns0:hi> the King of <ns0:hi>Persia.</ns0:hi> This judgment which he telleth them should be by the Sword, he expresseth by the effects, <ns0:hi>falling</ns0:hi> and rising <ns0:hi>no more,</ns0:hi> and commands them to <ns0:hi>drink</ns0:hi> it to comport, with the metaphor of the Wine cup of Gods fury, mentioned <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 15. The drinking of cups of heady intoxicating Wine ordina<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rily producing such effects, as <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>puing</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>falling,</ns0:hi> &c. This cup of the Lords fury he assures them, they should not turn by, but should most certainly drink it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 For lo, I begin to bring evil <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 11.31. chap. 49.12. Ezek. 9.6. Obad. 16. Luk. 23.31.</ns0:note> on the city which is <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>upon which my name is called.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> called by my name, and should ye be utterly unpunished <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">By the City called by his name; or upon which his name was called, he means <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> elsewhere called the <ns0:hi>Holy City.</ns0:hi> The Apostle 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.17. Speaketh much to this purpose, <ns0:hi>The time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God, and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the Gospel of God.</ns0:hi> If God spareth not the green Tree, how shall he spare those that are dry and withered? Atheists, and leud and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fane Persons have little reason to promise themselves an escape from Gods righteous judgment, when they see God not sparing those that make the highest profession of him, and stand in some relation to him.</ns0:note>? ye shall not be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />punished: for I will call for a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">It is in vain for you to promise your selves an escape, for God is about to punish all your neigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bours.</ns0:note>, saith the LORD of hosts.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 Therefore prophesie thou against them all these words, and say unto them <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Reveal my will unto them presently to revenge my self up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on them, in words to this sense or purpose, tell them, that I who hitherto have been toward them as a Lamb will now be to them as a Lion, so <ns0:hi>Ioel</ns0:hi> 3.16. <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> 1.2. and 3.8. and, as a Lion, will roar from Heaven, for though the Temple be some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times so called, yet the foregoing words <ns0:hi>from</ns0:hi> on high expound this term in this place otherwise.</ns0:note>, The LORD shall roar from on high, and utter his voice from his holy habitation <ns0:hi>i,</ns0:hi> he shall mightily roar upon his habitation <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Or <ns0:hi>in his habitation</ns0:hi> which is more likely to be understood <ns0:hi>in Heaven,</ns0:hi> (as the former,) then in <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> as divers would have it, for God is here re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vealing his wrath against forreign Nations, upon some of which these judgments came after God had done roaring in or upon <ns0:hi>Ierusalem.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, he shall give a shout, as they that tread <ns0:hi>the grapes,</ns0:hi> against all the inhabitants of the earth <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">A shout, such as Souldiers use to give when they storm a City, or assault their Enemies to incourage their fel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowes, and to dishearten their Enemies, like the shout of those that tread the Grapes, singing one to another, or rejoycing and triumphing in the <ns0:hi>Vintage.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 A noise shall come <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> to the ends of the earth, for the LORD hath a controversie with the nations <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">There shall be such confusions and noises, as shall ring over all the World, for Gods quarrel is not against the Jews only, but other Nations also.</ns0:note>: he will plead with all flesh <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Nor will be in any thing he doth, act injustly, if they will join issue with him he will plead with them, and make it appear to all that he acteth righteously.</ns0:note>, he will give them that are wicked to the sword <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">He will give up many to the Sword, but they shall be such onely as by their wickedness have deserved it, recompensing to them their own works and evil doings.</ns0:note>, saith the LORD.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Behold, evil shall go forth from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind shall be raised up, from the coasts of the earth <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">It is much the same thing which was said before, onely re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peated for the greater terrour in a variety of expressions. He tells them that the judgment should be like a contagion, going from one Nation to another, or like a fire catching hold of ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther house before the first is burned down, like a <ns0:hi>whirlwind</ns0:hi> that blows from all sides, cometh suddenly, and devoureth dread<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fully.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And the slain of the LORD shall be at that day from <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> end of the earth even unto the <ns0:hi>other</ns0:hi> end of the earth: they shall not be <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 16.4.</ns0:note> lamented, neither gathered nor buried, they shall be dung upon the ground <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">That t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ose who should be slain by commission from the Lord in this time of his judgments, should be in all places, and so numerous, that there should be none left to lament for, or to bury the dead, but the dead bodies should lye and rot upon the surface of the earth, and be as muck to it. See the like phrases <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.4.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 ¶ <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 4.8. and 6.26.</ns0:note> Howl ye shepherds and cry, and wallow your selves <ns0:hi>in the ashes,</ns0:hi> ye principal of the flock <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Shepherds</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>principal of the flock,</ns0:hi> are in this place of the same significancy, by both he means the civil Rulers, so the word is used <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 22.22. and 23.1. These he calls afore<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hand to bewail their face.</ns0:note>: for <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>your days for slaughter.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> the days of your slaughter, and of your dispersions are accomplished <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">For the days were now come, when they should be slain and scattered.</ns0:note>, and ye shall fall like <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>vessel of desire.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> a plesant vessel <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">And he tells them their fall should be like the fall of a chrystal glass, or some de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />licate tender vessel<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> wh<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ch when it falleth breaketh in pieces and cannot again be set together.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>flight shall perish from the shepherds and escaping from,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note> the shepherds shall have no way to flee, nor the principal of the flock to escape <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">In ordinary dispensations of judgment<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> there is some way left to escape<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and if there be any way of escape<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> great men are likeliest to find it, but he telleth them that the greatest men should find no way to flee from or escape this terrible dispensa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 A voice of the cry of the shepherds, and an howling of the principal of the flock <ns0:hi>shall be heard</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">That is there shall be heard a great outcry of the Princes, and Rulers.</ns0:note>: for the LORD hath spoiled their pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sture <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">When they shall see how the Lord hath spoiled the Cities in which, and their people upon which they have lived, and amongst whom they were wont to feed securely.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 And the peaceable habitations are cut down because of the fierce anger of the LORD <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">That is, the places where these great men were wont to live splendidly, and dwell peaceably and securely <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>hall be as surely destroyed through the Lords anger, as if it were already done.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 He hath forsaken <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 4.7.</ns0:note> his covert as the li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">God had before compared himself to a Lion, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 30. here he declares himself to be about to move like a Lion, who when he goeth out to seek his prey, leaveth his covert, vide <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 50.44.</ns0:note>: for their lands is <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>a desol<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> desolate, because of the fierceness of the oppressor, and because of his fierce anger <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The effects of this rising up of God out of his covert is the desolation of the Land through the fierceness of the Enemy, caused from the fierce anger of God now ready to be poured out upon this people.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
